passages.title: BC Hansard 2026-05-28 pm, Issue 188 (Komoks Treaty Act third reading, Conservative speeches)
passages.quote: David Eby : We have heard, from small business, concerns about chronic property offending, repeat shoplifters, vandalism, arson — issues like that. The member will know that we initiated a program around repeat violent offenders, the ReVOII program. We’re continuing to support that program. Because of the success of that program either deterring people from offending or ensuring that they are behind bars, we have, in this budget, expanded to the new chronic property offending intervention initiative.

passages.quote: Nina Krieger : I appreciate the question and want to make it very clear that police in British Columbia enforce the law. This government is committed to providing police with the tools that they need to engage with the challenges of our time. That’s why we have made a historic investment in policing in our province — over $230 million, hiring 256 officers, with an emphasis on rural and remote communities. That’s why we’ve increased training for police, and that’s why we are standing up dedicated programs to provide police with the tools to go after repeat violent offenders and property crime, which we know are causing such challenges in our communities.

passages.quote: The PST on security, along with other services — recognizing the shift in our economy towards services — enables us to be able to put resources like $16 million into the chronic property offending initiative; $26 million into the repeat violent offending initiative; $14 million over two years to support the special investigation and targeted enforcement programs; $10 million over two years for community safety and targeted enforcement, the CSTEP program, which has included shoplifting crackdowns in different communities. The goal here is to reduce offences and improve community safety.
